source.section: Schedule 1S lines 3, 4 and 27, the Worksheet for Pension Income Deduction lines P1-P10 and the Worksheet for Phaseout of Non-Military Pension Income Deduction lines 1-5 (Schedule 1S PDF p.2); booklet Schedule 1S line 3 (PDF p.7) and line 4 (PDF p.8); Form 1040ME lines 14-20; line 17 chart and Worksheet for Standard / Itemized Deductions lines 1-8 (booklet PDF p.5); line 18 (PDF p.5); 2025 Tax Rate Schedules (PDF p.13). Record cite: pension_income_deduction, PDF page 8, 36 M.R.S. 5122(2)(M-2); income_test width 100,000 (50,000 married filing separately) and share to four decimals from the phaseout worksheet lines 4 and 5 (Schedule 1S PDF p.2)

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 115,083.00 + private pension (person 0) 40,000.00 = 155,083.00. Federal taxable income = 155,083.00 - 15,750.00 standard deduction = 139,333.00 (federal senior deduction ignored). Form 1040ME, single: line 14 federal AGI 155,083.00. Schedule 1A line 1 (PDF p.7) other-state municipal bond interest 0.00; Schedule 1A total = line 15a 0.00. Schedule 1S line 3 (PDF p.7) taxable Social Security 0.00 + railroad retirement 0.00 = 0.00. Worksheet for Phaseout of Non-Military Pension Income Deduction (Schedule 1S PDF p.2): line 1 federal AGI 155,083.00; line 2 125,000.00; line 3 30,083.00; line 4 100,000.00; line 5 = 30,083.00 / 100,000.00 = 0.30083, entered to four decimals as 0.3008. Pension Income Deduction Worksheet (taxpayer column, person 0, age 62): P1 eligible non-military pension income 40,000.00; P2 48,216.00; P3 Social Security and railroad benefits received 0.00; P4 = 48,216.00 - 0.00 = 48,216.00; P5 smaller of P1 and P4 = 40,000.00; P6 0.3008; P7 = 40,000.00 x 0.3008 = 12,032.00; P8 = 27,968.00; P9 military retirement pay 0.00; P10 = 27,968.00. Schedule 1S line 4 = P10 total 27,968.00 (non-military 27,968.00 + military 0.00). Schedule 1S line 27 total subtractions = 0.00 + 27,968.00 = line 15b 27,968.00. Line 16 Maine AGI = 155,083.00 + 0.00 - 27,968.00 = 127,115.00. Line 17 (person 0 born 1963-03-30 is 62 at December 31, 2025; 0 box(es)): Worksheet for Standard/Itemized Deductions (PDF p.5): line 1 127,115.00; line 2 100,000.00; line 3 27,115.00; line 4 75,000.00; line 5 = 0.361533..., entered to four decimals as 0.3615; line 6 chart amount 15,000.00; line 7 = 15,000.00 x 0.3615 = 5,422.50; line 8 = 9,577.50. Projection (share kept 1 - 0.3615 = 0.6385): base 15,000.00 x 0.6385 = 9,577.50, the same. Line 17 = 9,577.50. Line 13 = 1; line 18 exemption = 1 x 5,150.00 = 5,150.00 (Maine AGI not over 333,450.00). Line 19 taxable income = 127,115.00 - 9,577.50 - 5,150.00 = 112,387.50. Line 20 tax from the rate schedule (PDF p.13): 5.8% x (26,800.00 - 0.00) = 1,554.40 + 6.75% x (63,450.00 - 26,800.00) = 2,473.875 + 7.15% x (112,387.50 - 63,450.00) = 3,499.03125 = 7,527.30625, 7,527.31 to the cent. The printed schedule (PDF p.13) with its whole-dollar constant 4,028.00 gives 7,527.03; expected keeps the bracket tax computed in full. Line 23 nonrefundable credits 0.00; line 24 Maine income tax 7,527.31. Without the four-decimal rounding the share would be 0.30083 and P7 12,033.20; the worksheet's 0.3008 gives 12,032.00.
accepted_approximations: Tax is computed from the rate schedules as numbers. The booklet's table taxes 100-dollar rows and the printed schedule constants are rounded to dollars.
